questions.question: A train running at 26.5 km/h takes 18 s to pass a platform. Next, it takes 12 s to pass a man walking at 5 km/h in the opposite direction. Find the length of the platform.
questions.solution:
Given:

A train running at 26.5 km/h takes 18 s to pass a platform.

Next, it takes 12 s to pass a man walking at 5 km/h in the opposite direction.

Concept used:

Relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds while two bodies are coming from the opposite direction.

1m/s = 18/5 km/h

Time × Speed = Distance

Calculation:

Total distance = 26.5 × 5/18 × 18 = 132.5 m

Hence, the relative speed of the train and the person

⇒ 26.5 + 5 = 31.5 km/hr

Length of train = 31.5 × 5/18 × 12

⇒ 105 m

Thus, the length of the platform = 132.5 - 105 = 27.5 m

∴ The length of the **platform** is 27.5 m.

questions.question: Two trains 320 m and 205 m in length are running towards each other on parallel lines. One train runs at the rate of 70 kmph and the other train runs at the rate of 56 kmph. Find the time they will take to cross each other (in seconds).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two trains 320 m and 205 m in length are running towards each other on parallel lines. 

Speed of the two trains are 70 kmph and 56 kmph, respectively

**Concept used:**

When two objects run in opposite directions then their relative speed = Sum of their speeds

**Calculation:**

Relative speed of the trains = 70 + 56 = 126 km/h

Relative speed of the train in m/s = 126 × (5/18) = 35 m/s

Required time taken to cover the distance = (320 + 205) ÷ 35 = 525 ÷ 35

⇒ 15 seconds

**∴ The time they will take to cross each other is 15 (in seconds).**

questions.question: Two trains that are 125 metres and 99 metres in length, respectively, are running in opposite directions at the speeds of 40 km/h and 32 km/h, respectively. In how much time will they be completely clear of each other from the moment they meet?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of trains = 125 m and 99 m 

Speed of trains = 40 km/h and 32 km/h

**Formula used:**

Speed = (Distance)/(Time)

1 km/h = **(5)/(18)** m/s

**Calculations:**

Total distance travelled by both the trains = 125 + 99 = 224 m

Total speed of both the trains (km/h) = 40 + 32 = 72 m 

⇒ Total speed of both the trains (m/s) = 72 × (5)/(18)

⇒ Total speed of both the trains (m/s) = 20

Time taken = (Total Distance)/(Total Speed)

⇒ Time taken = (224)/(20)

⇒ Time taken = 11.2 s

**∴ The time taken is 11.2 seconds.**

questions.question: If Tanya walks at the speed of 6 km/h, she misses a train by 2 minutes. However, if she walks at the speed of 8 km/h, she reaches the station 3 minutes before the arrival of the train. The distance covered by Tanya to reach the station is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed1 (S1) = 6 km/h

Speed2 (S2) = 8 km/h

Time difference at S1 = 2 minutes = 2/60 hours

Time difference at S2 = 3 minutes = 3/60 hours

**Formula used:**

Distance (D) = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

Let D be the distance.

At 6 km/h:

Time1 = D/S1 + 2/60

At 8 km/h:

Time2 = D/S2 - 3/60

⇒ Time1 = Time2

⇒ (D)/(6) + (2)/(60) = (D)/(8) - (3)/(60)

⇒ (D)/(6) - (D)/(8) = -(3)/(60) - (2)/(60)

⇒ (D)/(6) - (D)/(8) = -(5)/(60)

⇒ (4D - 3D)/(24) = -(1)/(12)

⇒ (D)/(24) = -(1)/(12)

⇒ D = 2 km

**∴ The distance covered by Tanya to reach the station is 2 km.**

questions.question: A train of length 300 metres crosses a tree in 20 seconds and crosses another train of the same length travelling in opposite direction in 25 seconds. What is the speed of the second train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed of the first train = Distance ÷ Time = 300 ÷ 20 = 15 m/s

Relative speed of both trains (opposite direction) = Total Distance ÷ Time = (300 + 300) ÷ 25 = 600 ÷ 25 = 24 m/s

Speed of the second train = Relative Speed − Speed of first train = 24 − 15 = 9 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 9 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7fe2cb9f8b0b10992f5f16c8700501c9f9a876b4fdc5916368e2d0baba0e4e17.png] 

**Given:**

Length of Train 1 (L₁) = 300 m

Time to cross a tree = 20 s

Length of Train 2 (L₂) = 300 m

Time to cross each other = 25 s

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Relative speed in opposite direction = S₁ + S₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of Train 1 (S₁) = 300 ÷ 20 = 15 m/s

⇒ Total distance to cross each other = L₁ + L₂ = 300 + 300 = 600 m

⇒ Relative speed = Total Distance ÷ Crossing Time

⇒ S₁ + S₂ = 600 ÷ 25

⇒ 15 + S₂ = 24

⇒ S₂ = 24 − 15

⇒ S₂ = 9 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 9 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two trains travel in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: S = S₁ − S₂ (where S₁ > S₂).

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two trains travel towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: S = S₁ + S₂.

Crossing a Stationary Object

If a train crosses a pole, standing man, or tree, the distance covered is equal to the length of the train alone: D = L₁.

Crossing a Platform/Bridge

If a train crosses a platform or another train, the total distance covered is the sum of their lengths: D = L₁ + L₂.

questions.question: A and B are two stations 420 km apart. A train starts from A at 11 am and travels towards B at the speed of 70 kmph. Another train starts from B at 12 noon and travels towards A at the speed of 30 kmph. At what time do they meet?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between stations A and B = 420 km

Speed of the train starting from A = 70 kmph

Speed of the train starting from B = 30 kmph

Train from A starts at 11 am

Train from B starts at 12 noon

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Let the trains meet after t hours from 12 noon.

Distance covered by the train from A in (t+1) hours (since it starts 1 hour earlier) = 70 × (t + 1)

Distance covered by the train from B in t hours = 30 × t

Since the total distance is 420 km, we have:

70(t + 1) + 30t = 420

⇒ 70t + 70 + 30t = 420

⇒ 100t + 70 = 420

⇒ 100t = 350

⇒ t = 3.5

So, the trains meet 3.5 hours after 12 noon, which is 3:30 pm.

**The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: Two trains, one 125 metres and the other 375 metres long are running in opposite directions on parallel tracks, at the speed of 81 km/hr and 63 km/hr respectively. How much time will they take to cross each other?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the first train = 125 metres

Length of the second train = 375 metres

Speed of the first train = 81 km/hr

Speed of the second train = 63 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Time is taken to cross each other = Total distance to be covered / Relative speed

**Solution:**

Total distance to be covered = Length of first train + Length of second train

= 125 metres + 375 metres

= 500 metres

Relative speed = Speed of first train + Speed of second train

= (81 km/hr + 63 km/hr) × (5/18) m/s [Converting km/hr to m/s]

= (144 × 5)/18 m/s

= 40 m/s

Time is taken to cross each other = Total distance to be covered / Relative speed

= 500 metres/40 m/s

= 12.5 seconds

**Therefore, the two trains will take 12.5 seconds to cross each other.**

questions.question: A train crosses a 400 m-long platform in 50 seconds. It crosses another 600 m-long platform in 60 seconds. What are the length and the speed of the train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken to cross 400 m long platform = 50 seconds

Time taken to cross another 600 m long platform = 60 seconds

**Concept used:**

Time = **(Distance)/(Speed)**

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the length of a train be x m

⇒ Putting the values in the formula,

⇒ 400 +x over 50 = 600 +xover 60

⇒ 60(400 + x) = 50(600 + x)

⇒ 24000 + 60x = 30000 + 50x

⇒ 10x = 6000

⇒ x = 600 metres

⇒ Speed = 400 + 600 over 50 = 20m/sec

⇒ For converting m / sec into km / h, multiply the value with (18)/(5)

⇒ So, 20 m / sec = 20times (18)/(5) = 72 km/h

** Hence, The length and speed of the train are 600 meters and 72 km/h respectively.**

questions.question: A 1800 metres long train crosses a man walking in opposite direction in 10 seconds. If the speed of train is 8 times to the speed of man, then what is the speed of train?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Length of train = 1800 meters,

Time taken = 10 seconds,

Ratio of speeds = 8:1

**Concept Used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

**Calculation:**

Total speed = Distance / Time = 1800 m / 10 s = 180 m/s (This is the relative speed)

Speed of train = 8/9 × total speed = 8/9 × 180 = 160 m/s

In km/hr, 160 × 18/5 = 576 km/hr

**Therefore the speed of the train is 576 km/hr.**

questions.question: A man walking at a rate of 4 km/h crossed a tunnel in 18 minutes. What is the length of the tunnel in meters?

Time taken by man = 18 min

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance/Time

1 km/hr = 5/18 m/s

1 min = 60 sec

**Calculation:**

Let the distance be x

Speed = Distance/Time

⇒ (4 × 5/18) = x/(18 × 60)

⇒ 20/18 = x/1080

⇒ 18x = 1080 × 20

⇒ 18x = 21,600

⇒ x = (21,600/18)

⇒ 1200 m

**∴ The length of the tunnel is 1200 m**
